s: Young lava field of scoria cones, maars and white domes · home of Al Wahbah
dr: Mostly Pleistocene; youngest cones younger than about 6,500–4,000 years ago
se: Around Al Wahbah lies a whole field of about 180 young volcanoes, some so fresh they erupted after the last green period of Arabia
sa: حول فوهة الوعبة يمتد حقل كامل من نحو 180 بركانًا فتيًّا، ثار بعضها بعد آخر فترة مطيرة عرفتها الجزيرة العربية
desc: Harrat Kishb is a volcanic field of about 5,900 km² in Makkah Province, with basaltic scoria cones, tuff rings and maars, and phonolitic lava domes and flows. Most of the field is Pleistocene; Holocene flows are limited to three areas in its western half, and the youngest products (Jabal Aslaj, Jabal Hil and Jabal Shalman) post-date a pluvial period of roughly 6,500–4,000 years ago. Jabal Hil is a large scoria cone whose 300 m wide crater was filled and overtopped by a lava lake, and its pahoehoe flow contains a lava tube up to 20 m wide. Kaminski & Garrison count about 180 volcanoes younger than two million years over roughly 60 × 90 km, including the Al Wahbah maar.
sig: The volcanic setting of the Al Wahbah crater and one of the youngest lava fields of western Arabia.
refs: Global Volcanism Program. Harrat Kishb (231071). Volcanoes of the World. Smithsonian Institution. https://volcano.si.edu/volcano.cfm?vn=231071
Kaminski, M.A. & Garrison, T.F. (2022). The Al Wahbah Crater of Saudi Arabia and its geotourism potential. Geotourism 3–4 (70–71). https://doi.org/10.7494/geotour.2022.3-4(70-71).3
conf: Coordinates are the Smithsonian GVP reference point for the field, about 27 km east of the Al Wahbah crater record. The GVP text gives the area as 5,900 km³; read here as km² as in the GVP image caption. Timeline: start set at 2 Ma from the ‘under two million years’ figure, end at the youngest dated limit

s: 40 km granite escarpment rising from Wadi Nu’man to Jabal Daka
dr: Granitic escarpment of the northern Asir mountains; Key Biodiversity Area
te: The granite wall above Makkah’s plain
se: West of Taif a granite wall climbs more than 2,000 m in a few kilometres, where two kinds of juniper meet
sa: غرب الطائف يرتفع جدار من الجرانيت أكثر من 2000 متر خلال كيلومترات قليلة، وعنده يلتقي نوعان من العرعر
desc: A granitic escarpment about 40 km long and 10 km wide on the west-facing edge of the northern Asir mountains, rising from about 500 m in Wadi Nu’man to some 2,600 m at the peaks of Jabal Daka and Jabal Barad. The higher slopes are moister, much of the ground is rocky, and a narrow wooded zone along the lip is the only place in Arabia where Juniperus phoenicia and J. excelsa overlap to any extent. GeoNames gives Jabal Dakah, on this escarpment, an elevation of 2,585 m. The area of about 371.9 km² is recognised as a Key Biodiversity Area.
sig: A clear example of the great Red Sea–facing escarpment of western Arabia, with a steep climatic and vegetation gradient.
refs: Key Biodiversity Areas Partnership. Taif escarpment (KBA 8275) factsheet. https://www.keybiodiversityareas.org/site/factsheet/8275
GeoNames. Highest mountains in Saudi Arabia. https://www.geonames.org/SA/highest-mountains-in-saudi-arabia.html
conf: Coordinates are the KBA central point. Main source is a biodiversity factsheet; geological detail is limited to ‘granitic escarpment’. Timeline is a broad estimate (Arabian Shield basement to present); the cited sources give no rock age

s: White Cambrian river sandstone with honeycomb weathering · major aquifer rock
te: The rock carved by wind into a honeycomb
se: North of Buraydah, white sandstone laid down by ancient braided rivers has been weathered into a honeycomb rock
sa: شمال بريدة، رمال بيضاء أرستها أنهار مضفّرة قديمة تحوّلت إلى صخرة نحتتها التجوية كقرص العسل
desc: Locality 3 of a geotourism route north of Buraydah exposes the Risha Member of the Saq Formation, of Upper Cambrian age. The rock is white quartz sandstone deposited in a non-marine setting, most likely by braided streams. The Saq sandstone is a major aquifer, and the outcrop known as ‘Antarah’s Rock’ shows honeycomb weathering and graffiti. Nearby, at Gaf Al Jewa, the Hirnantian Sarah Formation contains glaciofluvial siltstones and sandstones with iron-oxide concretions.
sig: An accessible view of the Cambrian sandstone that forms one of Arabia’s main groundwater aquifers.
ex: Kaminski et al. (2019); Alqubalee et al. (2023)
refs: Kaminski, M.A., Garrison, T.F. & Yoder, C.E. (2019). The Paleozoic formations of the Al-Qassim Province in Saudi Arabia as potential sites for geotourism. n: Old Qusaiba village and the Qusaiba Shale
s: Silurian graptolite shale beneath a mud-brick village · major petroleum source rock
dr: Qusaiba Formation, Lituigraptus convolutus Zone; Sharawra Formation above
te: The shale that made Arabia’s gas
ta: الطَّفَل الذي صنع غاز الجزيرة العربية
se: Below an abandoned mud-brick village lies dark Silurian shale full of graptolites, the rock that fed much of Arabia’s oil and gas
sa: تحت قرية طينية مهجورة يمتد طَفَل داكن من العصر السيلوري مليء بالجرابتوليت، وهو الصخر الذي غذّى كثيرًا من نفط الجزيرة العربية وغازها
desc: At Old Qusaiba village in Al-Qassim, the escarpment exposes shales of the Qusaiba Formation of Early Silurian (Aeronian, Lituigraptus convolutus Zone) age, overlain by sandstones of the Sharawra Formation with trace fossils. Kaminski et al. record 14 graptolite species and the oldest known Ammobaculites (lituolid foraminifera) here. The Qusaiba shale is a major petroleum source rock. Al-Laboun measured 42 m of Sharawra Formation at the Qusayba escarpment, where it rests disconformably on the Qusaiba Formation.
sig: An outcrop of the Silurian ‘hot shale’ that sourced much of the Palaeozoic hydrocarbons of Arabia, beside an abandoned mud-brick village.
refs: Kaminski, M.A., Garrison, T.F. & Yoder, C.E. (2019). The Paleozoic formations of the Al-Qassim Province in Saudi Arabia as potential sites for geotourism. Geotourism 3–4 (58–59). https://yadda.icm.edu.pl/baztech/element/bwmeta1.element.baztech-05b95701-f365-4131-864b-5213ec8c9426/c/geotour.2019.58-59.3.pdf

s: Ordovician sea-floor and glacial sandstones · some of the oldest multichambered foraminifera
dr: Ra’an and Quwarah members, Qasim Formation (Katian); Sarah Formation (Hirnantian)
el: Among the oldest multichambered agglutinated foraminifera
te: Where an ancient sea met the ice
se: On the edge of Buraydah, rocks record a deep Ordovician sea, then rivers of meltwater from the great ice age that followed
sa: على أطراف بريدة تروي الصخور قصة بحر أوردوفيشي عميق، ثم أنهار من مياه الذوبان خلّفها العصر الجليدي العظيم الذي تلاه
desc: Near Qassim University on the northern outskirts of Buraydah, the Ra’an Member of the Qasim Formation (Upper Ordovician, middle Katian) records a maximum flooding surface and contains some of the oldest known multichambered agglutinated foraminifera (Reophax, Subreophax), with Quwarah Member sandstones above. At Khashm al Madba’ah the shallow-marine Quwarah sandstones are unconformably overlain by glaciofluvial sandstones of the Hirnantian Sarah Formation. Both units carry ferruginous concretions, ferricretes and deformed iron-oxide layers, which Alqubalee et al. link to iron carried from the weathered Arabian Shield during the Hirnantian glaciation.
sig: A compact section from Late Ordovician sea to ice-age outwash, with a key early record of foraminiferal evolution.
ex: Kaminski et al. (2019); Alqubalee et al. (2023)
refs: Kaminski, M.A., Garrison, T.F. & Yoder, C.E. (2019). The Paleozoic formations of the Al-Qassim Province in Saudi Arabia as potential sites for geotourism. Arabic name is a careful transliteration. Timeline uses the international Katian–Hirnantian span as an estimate

s: Fenced rock with Thamudic inscriptions below an Ordovician cliff north of Buraydah
dr: Thamudic inscriptions (not dated in the source)
te: Messages carved under the black cliff
se: Travellers long ago carved Thamudic writing on a rock beneath a cliff of ancient sea-floor shale
sa: حفر مسافرون قدامى كتابات ثمودية على صخرة عند سفح جرف من طَفَل قاع بحر قديم
desc: Kaminski et al. record the Al-‘Asoudah archaeological site at their Locality 1 north of Buraydah: a fenced stone with Thamudic inscriptions at the foot of a cliff of the Middle Ordovician Hanadir Member. The same locality exposes Cambrian–Ordovician Saq trace fossils, Hanadir graptolite shales and the Hirnantian glacial sandstones of the Sarah Formation at Jal al Aswad, the type locality of the Sarah Ridge. Saudipedia lists Al-Asoudah among the rock art and inscription sites of Al-Qassim, with engravings of camels, ibexes, horses, human figures and handprints.
sig: A protected inscription site set within one of the key Palaeozoic geology localities of central Arabia.
disc: Beside the Sarah Formation type ridge

s: Ancient sea-floor phosphate rock mined at one of the world’s largest phosphate deposits
dr: Jalamid Formation, Turayf Group; mining since 2010
se: In the far north, layers made from the remains of sea creatures 60 to 70 million years old now feed the world’s farms
sa: في أقصى الشمال تمتد طبقات تكوّنت من بقايا كائنات بحرية عمرها 60 إلى 70 مليون سنة، وهي اليوم تغذّي مزارع العالم
desc: The Al-Jalamid phosphate mining area lies in the Hazm Al-Jalamid quadrangle (31°–32°N, 39°–40°30′E) in northern Saudi Arabia, where the Jalamid Formation of the early Tertiary Turayf Group consists mostly of pelletal phosphorite, dolomitic limestone and limestone deposited in a shallow sea. Alhawsawi et al. state that the phosphate formed from organic remains roughly 60–70 million years ago; raw ore contains about 20–25% P2O5 and mining began in 2010. In the Sirhan–Turayf basin the Thaniyat Phosphorite Member at the base of the Jalamid Formation is Late Cretaceous, with calcareous phosphorite averaging about 32% P2O5.
sig: Described as one of the largest phosphate reserves in the world and a basis of Saudi Arabia’s fertiliser industry.
ex: Alhawsawi et al. (2021); Zhang et al. (2021); USGS MRDS
refs: Alhawsawi, A.M., Shababa, E.I., Qutub, M.M.T., Banoqitah, E.M. & Kinsara, A.A. (2021). Radiological characterization of the phosphate deposit in Al-Jalamid phosphate mining area, Saudi Arabia. Nukleonika 66(1), 35–44. https://doi.org/10.2478/nuka-2021-0005

n: Devonian microbial reefs of Dumat al-Jandal
na: الشعاب الميكروبية الديفونية في دومة الجندل
s: 405-million-year-old microbial reef mounds in the Qasr Member of the Jauf Formation
dr: Qasr Member, Jauf Formation (late Pragian–early Emsian, about 405 Ma)
el: Composite reefs up to about 10 m high and 60 m across
se: Near Marid Castle, round reef mounds were built 405 million years ago not by corals but by mats of microbes
sa: قرب قلعة مارد، شيّدت حُصُر من الميكروبات، لا المرجان، تلالًا مستديرة من الشعاب قبل 405 ملايين سنة
desc: Around Dumat al-Jandal the Qasr Member of the Jauf Formation, about 20 m of limestone of late Pragian to early Emsian age (about 405 Ma), contains microbial patch reefs. Individual reefs are circular to elliptical, 1–6 m high and up to 15 m across, while composite buildups reach about 10 m high and 60 m across; their cortices are stromatolites, thrombolites and leiolites, and they lack identifiable metazoan builders. At this locality, about 4 km north-west of Marid Castle, an escarpment exposes numerous bioherms, one of them about 25 m across. The wider Jauf Formation, about 287 m thick, also yields fish remains and fragments of the giant Devonian organism Prototaxites.
sig: Rare, well-exposed Early Devonian reefs built mainly by microbes on the northern margin of Gondwana.
ex: Matysik et al. (2015); Breuer et al. (2015)
refs: Matysik, M., Al-Ramadan, K. & Riding, R. (2015). Composition and morphology of Early Devonian microbial and metazoan patch reefs: Qasr Member of the Jauf Formation, northwestern Saudi Arabia. Journal of Sedimentary Research 85, 45–61. https://doi.org/10.2110/jsr.2015.04

conf: Coordinates are Locality 5 of Matysik et al. (2015), chosen to stay distinct from the Marid Castle record (Locality 1 lies just below the castle). Timeline is an estimate around the ~405 Ma age given in the source

s: Escarpment of Early Devonian braided-river sandstone up to 235 m thick
dr: Tawil Formation type section, At Tawil escarpment
se: South-west of Al-Jawf, a long north-facing cliff shows the sands of wide braided rivers that crossed Arabia about 400 million years ago
sa: جنوب غرب الجوف يكشف جرف طويل مطلّ على الشمال رمال أنهار مضفّرة واسعة عبرت الجزيرة العربية قبل نحو 400 مليون سنة
desc: The type section of the Tawil Formation lies on a north-facing escarpment at At Tawil in the Al Jawf quadrangle, where neither the upper nor the lower contact is exposed and the formation reaches a maximum thickness of 235 m. The Tawil is Early Devonian in age. Outcrop studies in the Jauf area describe it as stacked, cross-bedded sand bodies with minor mudstone, deposited by high-energy braided streams. It lies below the Jauf Formation and above the Silurian Sharawra Formation, on which it rests unconformably.
sig: The reference outcrop for a major Devonian sandstone unit of northern Arabia, used as a reservoir analogue.
ex: Meissner et al. (USGS, 1989); Osman et al. (2019)
refs: Meissner, C.R. Jr., Dini, S.M., Farasani, A.M., Riddler, G.P., Van Eck, M. & Aspinall, N.C. (1989). Preliminary geologic map of the Al Jawf quadrangle, sheet 29D, Kingdom of Saudi Arabia. U.S. Geological Survey Open-File Report. https://pubs.usgs.gov/of/1989/0342/report.pdf

s: Newly named Early Oligocene marine limestone recording the Eocene–Oligocene boundary
te: The sea that came back at the end of the greenhouse
ta: البحر الذي عاد في نهاية العصر الدافئ
se: East of Al-Qurayyat, a cliff of limestone holds tiny fossils from the moment Earth slid from a hot world into a cooler one
sa: شرق القريات يحفظ جرف من الحجر الجيري أحافير دقيقة من اللحظة التي انتقلت فيها الأرض من عالم حار إلى عالم أبرد
desc: The Qurayyat Formation was formally named in 2026 from sections in the Rashrashiyah area east of Al-Qurayyat, with its type section (Rash3) on a southern cliff near the quarry region. It is a Lower Oligocene marine limestone 15–26 m thick (about 26 m at the type section), resting with an erosional disconformity on the Middle–Upper Eocene Rashrashiyah Formation. The disconformity coincides with the extinction of the nannofossils Discoaster saipanensis and D. barbadiensis, and the study recorded 85 nannofossil species in 26 genera. The authors place the Eocene–Oligocene boundary at 33.9 Ma and infer a hiatus spanning part of zones NP19/20 and NP21.
sig: A new reference section in Arabia for the Eocene–Oligocene transition, one of the largest climate shifts of the Cenozoic.
refs: Aljahdali, M.H., Ghandour, I.M., Faris, M., Bantan, R.A., Alsaddah, M.M., Alrizqi, K.M., Wade, B. & El-Kahawy, R.M. (2026). Refined stratigraphical and biochronological framework of Paleogene successions in the northwest Arabian Plate. Rivista Italiana di Paleontologia e Stratigrafia 132(2), 269–293. https://doi.org/10.54103/2039-4942/30524

s: Southernmost young volcanic field of Saudi Arabia · erupted about 1810
te: The volcano that woke 200 years ago
se: Near the Red Sea coast of Jazan, small black cones erupted lava only about two centuries ago, and hot springs still bubble nearby
sa: قرب ساحل البحر الأحمر في جازان قذفت مخاريط سوداء صغيرة حممها قبل نحو قرنين فقط، وما زالت الينابيع الحارة تفور بالقرب منها
desc: Jabal Yar is a small olivine-basalt volcanic field on the Red Sea coast at the south-western tip of Saudi Arabia, described by the Smithsonian Global Volcanism Program as the southernmost young volcanic field in the country. It has three volcano groups, Qummatain, Djar’atain-Harra and ‘Ukwatain, and its highest point is 305 m. Hot springs occur south of Djar’atain and between Djar’atain and ‘Ukwatain. Its only recorded eruption, a small explosive eruption (VEI 2) with lava flows, is dated to 1810 ± 10 CE.
sig: One of the few Saudi volcanic fields with a historical eruption, close to Jazan’s towns.
refs: Global Volcanism Program. Jabal Yar (231080). Volcanoes of the World. Smithsonian Institution. https://volcano.si.edu/volcano.cfm?vn=231080
conf: Coordinates are the Smithsonian GVP reference point (17.05°N, 42.83°E). Arabic name is a transliteration. Timeline runs from the start of the Holocene (field age given only as Holocene) to the 1810 eruption

s: Isolated, terraced mountain massif rising from 500 to about 2,000 m
dr: Part of the Sarawat range; Key Biodiversity Area
te: The mountain of a thousand terraces
se: In Jazan a steep, lonely mountain rises straight from the lowlands, its slopes cut into farm terraces for coffee and maize
sa: في جازان يرتفع جبل شاهق منعزل مباشرة من الأراضي المنخفضة، وقد قُسّمت سفوحه إلى مدرّجات لزراعة البن والذرة
desc: Jabal Fayfa is an isolated, steep-sided mountain on the western side of the Asir mountains in Jazan Province, part of the Sarawat range. The Key Biodiversity Area covers about 122 km² between 500 and 2,000 m; its temperate summit is heavily built up and cultivated, and agricultural terraces on the slopes grow coffee and maize. The western slopes receive considerable rainfall, while juniper grows on slopes too steep to terrace. Saudipedia gives an elevation of 1,814 m for the mountain, about 100 km from Jazan city.
sig: A striking example of the Sarawat escarpment’s isolated massifs, shaped into one of Arabia’s best-known terraced landscapes.
refs: Key Biodiversity Areas Partnership. Jabal Fayfa (KBA 8286) factsheet. https://www.keybiodiversityareas.org/site/factsheet/8286
Saudipedia. Saudi Mountains. https://saudipedia.com/en/saudi-mountains
conf: Coordinates are the KBA central point. Summit heights differ between sources (about 2,000 m in the KBA factsheet, 1,814 m in Saudipedia). Timeline is a broad estimate (Arabian Shield basement to present); the cited sources give no rock age

s: Foothill wadi with Saudi Arabia’s main helmeted guineafowl population
se: East of Abu Arish, a green wadi with a small lake is the best place in Saudi Arabia for African birds such as the helmeted guineafowl
sa: شرق أبو عريش يُعد وادٍ أخضر فيه بحيرة صغيرة أفضل مكان في السعودية لطيور أفريقية مثل دجاج الوادي المُخوذ
desc: Wadi Jawwah is a sandy and clay wadi bed between steep volcanic slopes in the foothills east of Abu Arish, inland from Jizan, covering about 63.9 km² at 180–450 m. A small dam holds a lake for most of the year, and vegetation includes Dobera and Ficus trees with Acacia and Salvadora scrub. It is the most important site in Saudi Arabia for the helmeted guineafowl (Numida meleagris), with about 350 birds in 1988 and more than 1,000 in 1990, and has some of the country’s highest densities of breeding Afrotropical birds such as the bateleur. Autumn counts include 975 steppe buzzards and 650 steppe eagles on passage.
sig: A stronghold of Afrotropical birds in Saudi Arabia, traditionally protected by the local Emir.
refs: Key Biodiversity Areas Partnership. Wadi Jawwah (KBA 8288) factsheet. https://www.keybiodiversityareas.org/site/factsheet/8288
conf: Coordinates are the KBA polygon centre. Timeline starts from the KBA’s last assessment (1994). Arabic name is a careful transliteration. This place matches the must-have row ‘Wadi Jawwah / Wadi Jazan’ (no coordinates there); must_have left null as instructed for Part B

s: Vanished lake of the Empty Quarter where hippos lived and early humans camped
dr: Lake phases in MIS 5 (about 100,000 and 80,000 years ago) and the early Holocene (about 9,000–6,000 years ago)
el: Up to about 300 km² and 30 m deep
te: The lost lake of the Empty Quarter
se: Where dunes now stand, a lake up to 30 m deep once drew hippos, aurochs and early people to its shores
sa: حيث تقف الكثبان اليوم، كانت بحيرة يصل عمقها إلى 30 مترًا تجذب إلى شواطئها أفراس النهر والثيران البرية والبشر الأوائل
desc: Mundafan is a former lake on the south-western edge of the Rub’ al-Khali in Najran Province, occupying a wind-deflated basin of about 363 km² with up to about 24 m of sediment. High stands are dated to Marine Isotope Stage 5 (about 100,000 and 80,000 years ago) and to the early Holocene (about 9,000–6,000 years ago); at its maximum the lake covered about 300 km² and was about 30 m deep. Mussels, snails and stoneworts lived in the water, and aurochs, camels, gazelles, hippopotamuses and ostriches lived around it. Middle Palaeolithic and Neolithic sites around the old shorelines show repeated human occupation.
sig: Key evidence that the Empty Quarter was repeatedly green and open to human dispersal out of Africa.
ex: Crassard et al. (2013); Groucutt et al. (2015)
refs: Crassard, R. et al. (2013). Middle Palaeolithic and Neolithic Occupations around Mundafan Palaeolake, Saudi Arabia: Implications for Climate Change and Human Dispersals. PLOS ONE 8(7), e69665. https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0069665

Groucutt, H.S. et al. (2015). Human occupation of the Arabian Empty Quarter during MIS 5: evidence from Mundafan Al-Buhayrah, Saudi Arabia. Quaternary Science Reviews 119, 116–135. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.quascirev.2015.04.020
Wikipedia. Mundafan. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mundafan
conf: Coordinates (18°34′N, 45°20′E) and lake figures are taken from the Wikipedia summary of the cited papers; the papers themselves could not be opened, so verify against Crassard et al. (2013) before release. Arabic name follows common Arabic usage

s: The only Saudi lava field on the Red Sea shore · about 200 scoria cones
dr: Activity from the Miocene to Holocene cinder cones
te: Black lava meets the Red Sea
ta: حين تلتقي الحمم السوداء بالبحر الأحمر
se: South of Al-Birk, black lava flows and hundreds of cinder cones run right down to the Red Sea shore
sa: جنوب البرك تمتد مسايل الحمم السوداء ومئات المخاريط البركانية حتى شاطئ البحر الأحمر
desc: Harrat al-Birk, west of Abha, is the only Saudi volcanic field lying directly on the Red Sea coast and covers about 1,800 km², separating two coastal plains. Around 200 scoria cones have been identified; volcanism began in the Miocene and continued into the Holocene, and its Quaternary basalt to trachybasalt flows carry ultramafic inclusions. Németh counts 160 vents, eight of them phreatomagmatic, including Surtseyan-style tuff cones near the coast and a maar–tuff ring along Wadi Sabya. Freshly eroded ash around a vent at Jabal Ba’a suggests an eruption within the last century.
sig: A rare place where a young lava field meets the sea, recording both dry and water-driven eruptions.
disc: Only Saudi lava field on the coast
Possible eruption within the last century
refs: Global Volcanism Program. Harrat al-Birk (231072). Volcanoes of the World. Smithsonian Institution. https://volcano.si.edu/volcano.cfm?vn=231072

Németh, K. (2026). The Role of Phreatomagmatism in the Saudi Arabian Neogene–Quaternary Intra-plate Monogenetic Volcanism. In: Latest Advances in Volcanology – Volcanoes as Complex Geosystems. IntechOpen. https://doi.org/10.5772/intechopen.1016928
conf: Coordinates are the Smithsonian GVP reference point. Vent counts differ between GVP (about 200 cones) and Németh (160 vents). Timeline starts at the Miocene base (23 Ma) as an estimate and ends at the present because of the possible recent eruption

s: Highest summit in Saudi Arabia (3,015 m) on the crest of the Asir escarpment
se: At 3,015 m, Jabal Sawda is the highest point in Saudi Arabia, often wrapped in cloud above a sheer drop to the Tihama
sa: على ارتفاع 3015 مترًا يُعد جبل السودة أعلى نقطة في المملكة، وكثيرًا ما تلفّه الغيوم فوق منحدر حاد نحو تهامة
desc: GeoNames lists Jabal Sawda at 3,015 m as the highest mountain in Saudi Arabia, in ‘Asir Province. It stands on the crest of the west-facing Asir escarpment near Abha. On the adjoining Raydah escarpment the slope falls from 2,700 to 1,600 m in less than 3 km, with crags, permanent streams and frequent cloud cover. These cool, misty slopes carry largely intact Juniperus excelsa forest.
sig: The country’s highest summit and a classic viewpoint over the great escarpment of south-western Arabia.
disc: Escarpment drops about 1,100 m in 3 km
refs: GeoNames. Highest mountains in Saudi Arabia. https://www.geonames.org/SA/highest-mountains-in-saudi-arabia.html
Key Biodiversity Areas Partnership. Raydah escarpment (KBA 8282) factsheet. https://www.keybiodiversityareas.org/site/factsheet/8282
conf: Coordinates and elevation from GeoNames (gazetteer, 18.268°N 42.370°E). The site is about 8 km from the Raydah Reserve record but describes the summit, not the reserve. Timeline is a broad estimate (Arabian Shield basement to present); the cited sources give no rock age

s: One of the few permanent waterfalls in Saudi Arabia, in granite hills north of Abha
dr: Granite hill country; Key Biodiversity Area
se: High in the granite hills of Asir, a waterfall keeps flowing all year, a rare sight in the Arabian Peninsula
sa: في أعالي تلال عسير الجرانيتية يتدفق شلال طوال العام، وهو مشهد نادر في الجزيرة العربية
desc: Shallal ad-Dahna lies about 90 km north of Abha on the road to Taif, in broken granite hill country at about 2,400–2,700 m covered with juniper and acacia scrub. The site has one of the few permanent waterfalls in Saudi Arabia, with a pool. The Key Biodiversity Area of about 68.3 km² supports the isolated endemic Asir magpie (Pica pica asirensis) and frogs and toads that depend on permanent water. It is fully included in the protected-area system plan but faces grazing, drainage and visitor pressure.
sig: A rare perennial waterfall on the granite highlands of the Asir.
refs: Key Biodiversity Areas Partnership. Shallal ad-Dahna (KBA 8279) factsheet. https://www.keybiodiversityareas.org/site/factsheet/8279
conf: Coordinates are the KBA central point; the waterfall’s exact position is not published. Main source is a biodiversity factsheet. Timeline is a broad estimate (Arabian Shield basement to present); the cited sources give no rock age

s: World’s largest conventional offshore oil field, in the Arabian Gulf
te: An ocean of oil under the Gulf
se: Under the shallow Arabian Gulf lies the largest offshore oil field in the world, found in 1951
sa: تحت مياه الخليج العربي الضحلة يمتد أكبر حقل نفطي بحري في العالم، اكتُشف عام 1951
desc: Safaniya lies offshore in the Arabian Gulf about 225 km north of Dhahran, in water averaging about 22 m deep, and Aramco describes it as the world’s largest conventional offshore oil field. The structure was mapped as a ‘possible high area offshore’ in 1939, and the first offshore well, Safaniyah No. 1, was completed on 15 August 1951. Production began in April 1957 at about 50,000 barrels per day and passed 600,000 barrels per day in 1965. The field measures about 50 × 15 km, its main reservoir is the Cretaceous Safaniya sandstone of the Wasia Formation, and remaining oil was estimated at about 37 billion barrels (2019).
sig: A landmark of Arabian Gulf petroleum geology and Aramco’s first step offshore.
refs: Aramco (2026). Safaniyah: Aramco’s first step offshore. Elements magazine. https://www.aramco.com/en/news-media/elements-magazine/2026/safaniyah-aramcos-first-step-offshore
Global Energy Monitor. Safaniya Oil and Gas Field (Saudi Arabia). https://gem.wiki/Safaniya_Oil_and_Gas_Field_(Saudi_Arabia)
Wikipedia. Safaniya Oil Field. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Safaniya_Oil_Field
conf: Coordinates from Global Energy Monitor (marked exact) and Wikipedia (28.28°N, 48.75°E); the point is offshore. Reservoir age is given only as Cretaceous (Wasia Formation); the timeline is a broad mid-Cretaceous estimate

s: Giant oil field discovered in 1940, between Dhahran and Al-Hofuf
el: Estimated ultimate recovery about 16.3 billion barrels (2018)
se: Found in 1940, just as the Second World War began to slow work, Abqaiq became one of the giant oil fields of the Eastern Province
sa: اكتُشف حقل أبقيق عام 1940 حين كانت الحرب العالمية الثانية تُبطئ العمل، وصار من الحقول النفطية العملاقة في المنطقة الشرقية
desc: Abqaiq oil field lies in the Eastern Province between Dhahran and Al-Hofuf, about 48 km from Dhahran, with the Ghawar field to its west. Its first exploratory well was drilled in 1940, work was slowed by the Second World War, and three wells had been drilled by 1943, the first estimated at about 9,000 barrels per day. Production began in 1946. Global Energy Monitor gives an estimated ultimate recovery of about 18.5 billion barrels (2004 data) and 16.3 billion barrels (2018 data).
sig: One of the early giant discoveries that built the Saudi oil industry, next to Ghawar.
refs: Global Energy Monitor. Abqaiq Oil Field (Saudi Arabia). https://gem.wiki/Abqaiq_Oil_Field_(Saudi_Arabia)
Saudipedia. Abqaiq Oil Field. https://saudipedia.com/en/abqaiq-oil-field
conf: Coordinates from Global Energy Monitor (marked exact); Wikipedia gives a different point (25.93°N, 49.67°E). Era set to history because the sources give discovery dates but no reservoir age; timeline runs from discovery (1940) to the present
